parties:
MA Awal and another --------- Appellants
vs
Md Abdus Rashid Khan Chowdhury --------- Respondent
full_judgment: 4. Defendant Nos.1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint of the suit, contending, inter-alia, that the suit was not maintainable; it was barred by waiver, estoppel, and acquiescence and limitation. Their specific case, in short, is that defendant No.1 joined as Lecturer of Naogaon Degree College in 1962. Thereafter, he joined as Professor of Natore NS College. He started living in a rented house along with his wife situated at the northern side of the Madrasha. Mr AKM Naimul Ahsan, nephew of defendant No.2, got admission in Natore NS College. On the other hand, a son of Abdur Rouf Chowdhury of Chowdhury Bari also got admission in the said Natore NS College. Consequently, they became friends. At one stage, son of Abdur Rouf Chowdhury requested defendant No.1 to live in the disputed house which is undivided and belonged to Chowdhury family. Defendant No.1 was informed that the suit house is under care of Safia Mohabbat and that deeds to be reconstructed because of its dilapidated condition Abdur Rouf Chowdhury also informed him that defendant No.1 could live therein if he so desired by reconstructing the said house. He also asserted that after effecting final partition if Shafia Mohabbat gets the said homestead and decides to sell the same and then defendant No.1 can purchase the same. Accordingly, spending Taka 13,000, defendant No.1 reconstructed the disputed homestead. It has been also mentioned that the father-in-law of defendant No.1 i.e. the father of defendant No.2 Zahurul Islam was the founder Principal of Natore NS College. One Zamir Ali, Nayeb of Chowdhury family, disclosed to brother of defendant No.2 Sirajul Islam that Nuruzamman Khan Chowdhury has got the disputed premises by way of partition. Accordingly, Sirajul Islam, brother of defendant No.2 told defendant No.1 that said Nuruzzaman Khan Chowdhury would sell the said homestead. Learning this the defendants decided to purchase the said homestead and it was agreed with Nuruzzaman Khan Chowdhury that the suit property and structures thereon would be sold at a consideration of Taka 50,000. On 14-5-1983 said Nuruzzaman Khan Chowdhury executed 2 bainanamas on receipt of Taka 2500 + 2500 in favour of defendant Nos.1 and 2. Thereafter, defendant No.1 on 16-1-1985 got kabala deed registered on the basis of the said bainanamas in respect of 0.04 acre of land and premises thereon. Defendant No.2 got registration of the 0.04 acre of land from said Nuruzzaman Khan Chowdhury on 2-2-1985. That was done within the knowledge of the plaintiff. Nuruzzaman Khan Chowdhury had been living at Rajshahi Town, that is why the kabala deeds were registered at Rajshahi. The defendants are not monthly ejectable tenants under Nuruzzaman Khan Chowdhury and they did not pay any rent to him. Nuruzzaman Khan Chowdhury did not execute any bainanama in favour of the plaintiff. After purchase the defendants mutated their names in the khatian and paid rent to the Government. The kabala deed dated 26-8-1991 as obtained by the plaintiff is fraudulent because Nuruzzaman Khan Chowdhury transferred the suit property long before execution and registration of the deed of the plaintiff and by the said kabala deed dated 26-8-1991 the plaintiff did not acquire any title. The plaintiff has got no right, title and possession in the suit premises. As such the suit is liable to be dismissed.
